The closest match is not about picture descriptions. The supplied papers are about self-play reinforcement learning, hidden-information games, and social reasoning, including shared trunks or shared models in game settings, but none describes making image captions or using a moving average to create and check specific quality rules for picture descriptions [2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10].

One paper does mention an exponential moving average as a stronger deployment policy in self-play training, but it is for a game-playing agent, not image description quality checking [1]. Another uses a shared residual trunk with separate heads for an asymmetric board game, but again this is not about picture descriptions [2].
